text:
emma-gtn: heads-up — starting bring-up for phoenix9b (9B) as a cheaper longform summarization candidate. ran some int6 vs int8 slices and saw mixed results, want quick triage + recs.

alice-ml: quick summary of findings: int6 latency - 38ms/token, int8 - 54ms/token (server p3-like). quality (ROUGE-L on our news longform slice): int8=0.72, int6=0.69 average. but error mode is different: int6 cuts details at tails. :thinking:

bob-platform: nice. whats unit econ? tokens/sec and $/1M tokens?

alice-ml: rough unit econ (prod config we tested):
- phoenix9b-int8: 1.3M tokens/hr per GPU; ~$12 per 1M tokens
- phoenix9b-int6: 1.6M tokens/hr per GPU; ~$9.5 per 1M tokens (approx)
so ~20% cost savings but ~0.03 ROUGE-L drop on long summaries.

caroline-product: how visible will that 0.03 drop be to users? we care about extractive factuals and hallucination tail.

alice-ml: user-impact qualitatively: more likely to miss late-paragraph facts and some pronoun resolution errors in >800 token outputs. for short summaries (<150 tokens) diff is negligible.

dan-sre: perf and infra ask: any change in KV cache memory use / OOM risk with int6?

alice-ml: int6 reduces memory ~12% in our runtime (smaller activations), no OOM in current fleet configs. slightly higher throughput so watch for CPU-side batching bottlenecks.

quant-bot: eval snippet (sample gold vs model):
```
GOLD: "The committee approved the motion after a three-hour debate on infrastructure funding."
INT8: "The committee approved the motion after a three-hour debate on infrastructure funding."
INT6: "The committee approved the motion after the debate on funding."
```
(semantic compression on tail phrase -> minor loss of precision)

emma-gtn: ok. proposed operational approach?

bob-platform: propose hybrid routing + slice-based routing: default phoenix9b-int6 for eligibility then route to int8 or fallback when slice signals trigger (longform, high-precision queries). config example: 
```
routes:
  - match: {task: "long_summary", length_gt: 300}
    model: phoenix9b-int8
  - match: {tier: "default"}
    model: phoenix9b-int6
fallbacks:
  - on_regression: phoenix9b-int8
```

caroline-product: can we A/B for a week and run user-facing win/loss? need to show that cost saving doesn't hurt retention.

alice-ml: yes. recommended experiment: 10% traffic to int6 baseline, 10% to int8 baseline, 80% control (current 13B model). collect: ROUGE-L, faithfulness checks, and a small human eval on 200 examples for the longform slice. run for 7 days or 100k longform queries.

dan-sre: deployment checklist: monitor latency p95, error rate, memory, and model-fallback counts. add an alert: fallback_rate > 1% in 5m window -> rollback.

emma-gtn: final rec (ops + product): do hybrid rollout. holdback: pin 20% of cohort to int8 for first 2 weeks for sanity checks. if human eval delta < 0.02 ROUGE-L and no user regressions, escalate to +50% traffic and revisit unit econ. :thumbsup:

alice-ml: I'll post a short scorecard later with the per-slice numbers, config flags, and the eval artifact link. tagging @caroline-product @bob-platform for follow-ups.

caroline-product: thanks — would love the sample prompts that trigger failures so PMs can craft UX mitigations.

alice-ml: will add examples (tail-truncation cases) to the scorecard artifact.

quant-bot: automated note: eval job phoenix9b-int6-vs-int8-2026-02-12 completed. artifact: s3://redwood-eval/phoenix9b/2026-02-12/report.html

bob-platform: cool. :raised_hands: planning to flip up a canary with routing flags tomorrow morning.

emma-gtn: thanks team — thread complete for now.
